title: Family budget task
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y6 lesson 9 (Family budget task (pupil PDF, assessed))
intro: Lesson 9: Bills and tax; budget task and quiz. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Taxes
points: Income tax on earnings above a tax-free amount
VAT on many goods (20% standard rate)

model.title: Take-home pay £2000 a month. Bills £1200. Left?

parts.text: Left to spend on food and other costs: £500

questions.q: Add up the bills (rent, council tax, gas and electricity, water, internet and phones).
How much is left after the bills?
How much is left after food?
Share the £570 between sadaqah, saving, travel and other costs so the budget balances. Show that it adds up.
questions.a: For example: sadaqah £60, saving £300, travel £100, clothes and other £110 = £570. Any split that adds up to £570, includes sadaqah and saving, and puts needs first gets full marks.

questions.q: The washing machine breaks and costs £200 to fix. What would you change, and why?
questions.a: Take it from saving or other costs (for example saving £100 instead of £300), keeping bills, food and sadaqah; explain that needs come first.

keywords.def: money paid to the government to fund public services
a tax added to the price of many goods (20% standard rate)
money taken off pay before you receive it

questions.q: Core: Budget task (assessed): a family's monthly income, bills, food, saving and sadaqah must balance (pupil PDF).
questions.a: A balanced budget with essentials first.

questions.q: Extend: Explain what would happen if bills were not paid.
questions.a: Services could be cut off and debts would grow.

questions.q: A £10 item has 20% VAT added. Price?
Money quiz (portal, 6 questions): earning, value for money, riba, saving, bills and tax.
Big question: who pays for the NHS and roads?
